items.title: Max Verstappen takes pole for Las Vegas Grand Prix after Kimi Antonelli penalty
items.summary:
• Antonelli quickest in qualifying but will start from sixth

  • Verstappen on front row alongside Mercedes’ Russell

Kimi Antonelli was quickest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, but the newly-crowned world champion will not be on pole for Sunday’s race as he has a five-place grid penalty for taking a new engine for this meeting. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who was second, will take pole – his first in Las Vegas – and Mercedes’ George Russell will line up alongside him on the front row of the grid after finishing in third. Antonelli will start from sixth.

Lando Norris was fourth for McLaren and Isack Hadjar fifth for Red Bull. The Ferrari was not in good shape in Las Vegas however. Lewis Hamilton was struggling with a lack of grip throughout the session and could not hook up a good lap. Neither he nor his teammate Charles Leclerc could make it out of Q2, with Leclerc finishing in 11th and Hamilton in 12th. They will start from 10th and 11th after McLaren’s Oscar Piastri also has a 10-place penalty for taking a new engine.

items.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
items.summary:
The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player

Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.

He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.

items.title: Victor Wembanyama has turned his NBA finals humiliation into a revenge tour for the ages
items.summary:
After a humiliating NBA finals defeat, the 22-year-old has returned with a vengeance – and the Spurs look like contenders again

It wouldn’t be exactly right to say Victor Wembanyama didn’t miss a beat after a disastrous NBA finals in June that left him and his San Antonio Spurs defeated, memed and embarrassed. In the Spurs’ first game this season, against an Oklahoma City Thunder team since decimated by injuries, Wemby went an appalling 1-for-13 from the field. Ten of his 12 points came via free throws. After getting blocked by Aday Mara, he leaned over his knees and muttered furiously to himself as if trying to exorcise an intrusive thought. It brought to mind an image from the NBA finals a few months earlier: Wemby on the floor after being fouled by the Knicks’ Mitchell Robinson, crowing, “I’m in your head!” The Spurs went on to blow a 29-point lead, lose the game and the finals. Now Wemby seemed too preoccupied with the issues within his own dome to worry about wreaking havoc in anybody else’s.

Game two saw Wembanyama elect to lay the ball up instead of dunking it in the dying seconds of a close tilt with the Houston Rockets, which the springy Amen Thompson blocked spectacularly. Not a great start, and in a league whose narratives calcify long before sample sizes reach an adequate scale, it allowed for whispers that the Spurs were in trouble. But you could say Wembanyama has not missed…
items.t: Victor Wembanyama has turned his NBA finals humiliation into a revenge tour for the ages

items.title: Men’s tennis boosts prize money for players to more than $350m in major overhaul
items.summary:
• Cash increase via ATP’s creation of ‘One Vision’ company

  • More rest breaks added to reduce player welfare issues

The Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) has approved major changes to the financial structure of men’s tennis that will make the total prize money available to the players increase to more than $350m (£267m) by 2028, from $270m this year.

The creation of a new company to sell all the tour’s media, commercial and data rights, ATP Ventures, will lead to the investment of an additional $100m in player remuneration including an increased $50m bonus pool, a $25m year-end rankings bonus and $26m player pensions.

items.t: Major changes in men’s tennis will take prize money for players to more than $350m

items.title: Lewis Hamilton is now the apex sports protester as US athletes stay silent
items.summary:
The Ferrari driver has always used his fame to highlight causes he cares about. Now he stands out as other athletes tone down their rhetoric

Most Formula One drivers might slip away to the beach or the golf course on a week off between races. Lewis Hamilton is not most drivers, though. Instead he went to the Rafah border crossing between Egypt and Gaza. He greeted aid workers in Arabic, toured the checkpoint and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent warehouses in nearby El-Arish, where relief supplies are prepared for distribution. Hamilton made the visit on a day Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least seven Palestinians in Gaza, adding to a death toll that’s climbed above 74,000 since war broke out three years ago. He wore dark glasses and dressed head to toe in black.

“The past three years of Israel’s genocide in Gaza is appalling,” he wrote on Instagram of his visit, before turning the lens on himself. “I know so many people that feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than watch. I don’t want us to get used to their suffering. I don’t want us to look away.”

items.title: Rugby players face anxious wait as judges consider state of concussion case
items.summary:
• Players claim brain injury caused by negligence

  • Defendants want cases to be struck out due to delays

Hundreds of former rugby players taking legal action against the game’s governing bodies face an anxious wait to learn whether their cases will be allowed to proceed towards trial. The players allege they are suffering from neurological damage caused by the professional negligence of the defendants, World Rugby, the Rugby Football Union (RFU), the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) and the Rugby Football League.

After two days of hearings at the Royal Courts of Justice the presiding judges, Senior Master Cook and Mr Justice Cotter, retired to consider whether or not the case will be able to continue in anything like its current form.

items.title: Adam Hollioake being lined up for emotional return at Surrey as head coach
items.summary:
• Former captain has emerged as favourite to land post

  • Aaron Finch to be appointed as coach of MI London

Adam Hollioake is being lined up for a potential return to Surrey as head coach with Aaron Finch to be appointed as coach of MI London during a winter of change at the Oval.

While Surrey are running a formal recruitment process that remains open, it is understood the former captain is viewed internally as the favourite to replace Gareth Batty, who left after four years last month for an assistant coach’s job at the Chennai Super Kings.
